questions.a: An institutionalised framework of racial hierarchy and territorial segregation enforced by the minority European settler administration against indigenous non-white populations.

questions.a: The historical shift from minority racist governance to a multi-racial democratic order achieved through negotiation, forgiveness, and power-sharing agreements.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Democratic Transition and Constitution Making in South Africa'.

questions.a: The supreme foundational legal code of a sovereign territory establishing state structure, defining official authority, and securing civic protections.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Purpose and Core Functions of a Constitution'.
questions.a: A constitution generates trust among diverse groups by setting unalterable ground rules for government power and citizen entitlements.

concepts.title: Historical Precedents of the Indian Constitution

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Historical Precedents of the Indian Constitution' refers to.
questions.a: The progressive emergence of national constitutional principles through colonial-era reform bills, early freedom struggle drafts, and international democratic ideals.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Historical Precedents of the Indian Constitution'.
questions.a: Core democratic commitments such as adult franchise, equality, and minority protections were established well before the Constituent Assembly gathered.

questions.a: The opening declaration defining the source of authority and describing the essential political character of the Indian state.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Preamble: Nature of the Indian Sovereign Republic'.
questions.a: The Preamble asserts that ultimate authority stems from the people and defines the republic as sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic.
